rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate lexical account takes the earth's edges as arjāʾ, singular raja (maqṣūr) and dual rajawān.
rows.anchor: أرجاء الأرض واحدها رجا , مقصور , والاثنان رجوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired edges surround jinn and humans and herd them like quarry to be captured.
rows.anchor: فيحيطون بالجن والإنس فيحشرونهم حشر الصيد لإرادة أخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the day of display, a king reveals his throne, the seat of his dominion; the throne above them likewise manifests God's majesty.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الملك يظهر يوم العرض سرير ملكه ومحل عزه

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from al-Abbas describes eight horned beings, with the distance between their knees and hooves like that between heaven and earth; Biqāʿī takes them as individuals.
rows.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه , فظاهره أنهم أشخاص

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the bearers are four now and will be reinforced by four others at the Resurrection; al-Ṭabarānī transmits it through Ibn Isḥāq.
rows.anchor: هم اليوم أربعة فإذا كان يوم القيامة أيدهم بأربعة آخرين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Biqāʿī also notes that the number appears in the long Trumpet report transmitted by Abū Yaʿlā and others through a chain ending with Abū Hurayra; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: من طريق إسماعيل بن رافع عن يزيد بن زياد عن القرطبي عن رجل عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight could denote the occupants of the seven heavens and the Kursī, an uncountable creation; Biqāʿī says this best fits the display of divine greatness.
rows.anchor: أهل السماوات السبع والكرسي فتلك ثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, eight individuals could carry the throne; Biqāʿī calls this the clearest sense of the reports because their bearing it makes its immensity evident to onlookers.
rows.anchor: ويكون حملهم له أظهر في العظمة ليعلم كل من يرى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight exceeds seven, the conventional number of hyperbole, by one: however far one magnifies, the reality surpasses it, signaling limitless majesty and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى عدم الانتهاء والوقوف عند حد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fractions of eight (half, quarter, and eighth) total seven, which gathers odd, even, even-even, and even-odd numbers; this reinforces the image of boundless majesty.
rows.anchor: أن للثمانية من الكسور الصنف والربع والثمن , وذلك سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day's reality surpasses what eloquent speakers can convey, whether they soften or intensify their descriptions; this warning should make servants fear and seek salvation.
rows.anchor: فالأمر أعظم من مقالة قائل إن رقق البلغاء أو إن خفموا

rows.speaker: عبد الله الكفيف المالقي
rows.claim: A report cited through al-Dammāmīnī and al-Kindī says a sound Arab dialect inserts the conjunction wāw before eight in the counting sequence.
rows.anchor: عبد الله الكفيف المالقي أنها لغة فصيحة لبعض العرب أن يقول

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: A poem by one of the author's colleagues argues that seven completes the basic number types: one through four are foundational, while later numbers recombine them.
rows.anchor: بعض أصحابنا في كون السبعة منتهى العدد

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الكريم الشهرستاني
rows.claim: Al-Shahrastānī says number begins at two, with three and four the first odd and even; later numbers are compounds, making seven (three plus four) the complete endpoint and eight a new cycle.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام محمد بن عبد الكريم الشهرستاني في مقدمة كتابه الملل والنحل

rows.speaker: أبو الحكم ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjān offers another arithmetic account: six is the endpoint of number and seven is its witr, or single odd counterpart.
rows.anchor: أبو الحكم ابن برجان في تفسير سورة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī moves from warning about the Day of Calling to its general scene, the presentation, and then its particular division between beneficent and sinful people.
rows.anchor: فالعامة العرض , والخاصة التقسيم إلى محسن ومسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means on that day, when the events just described have taken place.
rows.anchor: أي إذا كان ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is passive because the presentation itself is terrifying and because the statement comes from the Almighty.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المهول نفس العرض , بنى فعله للمفعول ولأنه كلام القادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being presented to God for account is likened to a ruler reviewing troops to select the good for honor, nearness, and reward, and the corrupt for removal and punishment; the part stands for the whole accounting.
rows.anchor: كما يعرض السلطان الجند لينظر في أمرهم ليختار منهم المصلح للإكرام والتقريب والإثابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing about anyone is hidden from anyone that day, neither deeds nor selves, however subtle; complete disclosure from graves and hearts magnifies the saved person's happiness and the wicked person's misery.
rows.anchor: أي في ذلك اليوم على أحد بوجه من الوجوه الخفاء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو موسى رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā says there are three presentations: the first two involve disputation and excuses, while at the third the records fly out and people take them in the right or left hand.
rows.anchor: قال أبو موسى رضي الله عنه : هي ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's aim is to show God's complete power to destroy those warned and replace them with better people, and to bring about the Resurrection that they deny; Noah's story establishes the threat through his people's destruction for rejecting him.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على تمام القدرة على ما أنذر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as wholly perfect in majesty and generosity, universally giving outward blessings as al-Raḥmān, and granting His obedient allies lasting blessing as al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال كله من الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī calls qad a particle of expectation here: God has repeatedly bestowed benefits beyond others' power, demonstrating His complete ability and making faith due.
rows.anchor: فقال آتيا بحرف التوقع لأنه مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṭwār means successive stages: elements, compounds nourishing animals, humors, sperm, clots, chewed flesh, bones, flesh, nerves, and blood, then a complete speaking human in varied sexes and appearances.
rows.anchor: أي تارات عناصر أولا ثم مركبات تغذي الحيوان ثم أخلاطا ثم نطفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever could originate humans can recreate them even more readily; their wondrous formation proves they were not made in vain, so God must resurrect them to settle injustice and manifest wisdom, justice, honor, and favor.
rows.anchor: ومن قدر على هذا الابتداء كان على الإعادة أعظم قدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the oppressed may die without redress while an oppressor reaches his aims, resurrection is necessary for judgment; leaving matters unresolved would be a deficiency in God's dominion, and the able creator can recompense with reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا بد أن يعيدهم ليفصل بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After signs in human beings, the sūra turns to the greater cosmic signs, divided into upper and lower realms; it begins with the self as the nearest noble object of observation, then the heavens.
rows.anchor: بعد التذكير بما في أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens are supremely elevated, spacious, well-ordered, and adorned; their adornments make their sevenfold number recognizable.
rows.anchor: هي في غاية العلو والسعة والإحكام والزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭibāqan means layered and matching: each heaven lies above and encompasses the next; complete enclosure leaves no fissures, a correspondence too difficult for any other agent.
rows.anchor: أي متطابقة بعضها فوق بعض وكل واحدة في التي تليها محيطة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is in the lowest heaven; it is mentioned first for its nearness, quick motion through all stations monthly, disappearance on moonless nights, and reappearance, all wondrous signs of power.
rows.anchor: أي الذي ترونه وهو في السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīhinna refers to all the heavens; the moon's bright, spreading light reveals visible things, illuminating earth on one side and the heavens on the other.
rows.anchor: أحد وجهيه يضيء لأهل الأرض والثاني لأهل السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is in the fourth heaven; as a lamp it gives great light that dispels the night darkness from the earth.
rows.anchor: سراجا * } أي نورا عظيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, and al-Ṭabarī report from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that the sun and moon face the heavens and turn their backs toward earth; al-Ḥākim reports the moon wording.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are signs for seeing God in Paradise: everyone sees them unobstructed from their place, just as believers will see God directly after knowing Him through faith and reflection.
rows.anchor: آية على رؤية عباده المحسنين له في الجنة فإنه يرى كل أحد كلا من مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the heavens, Biqāʿī returns to human creation, the greatest created thing and clearest sign of God, now specifying its details while explicitly establishing resurrection through a plant-growth metaphor.
rows.anchor: أعاد الدلالة بخلق الإنسان لأنه أعظم المحدثات وأدلها على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grew humans from earth by creating their father Adam; the plant image recalls Adam's earthly origin and humanity's formation from earth.
rows.anchor: أي بخلق أبيكم آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth also supplies human food; people grow through that nourishment from the same earth from which they were created.
rows.anchor: من الأرض التي خلقنا منها , وبذلك الغذاء نمونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabātan is a verbal noun used where the verb would ordinarily appear; stripping the augmented form signals how easy this creative origination is for God despite its wondrous novelty.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى هوانه عليه سبحانه وتعالى وسهولته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses iḥtibāk: anbatakum implies a deleted first verbal noun, while the explicit second noun implies a deleted second verb, yielding anbatakum inbātan fa-nabattum nabātan.
rows.anchor: دال على حذف فعله أولا , ليكون التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning people to earth is gradual, through death and burial, even if their lifespans are long; death is accepted and undisputed, unlike the disputed initial creation argument.
rows.anchor: الأرض بالموت والإقبار وإن طالت الآجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings people out of the earth through resurrection; the verbal noun following the verb stresses the care taken to ensure its occurrence because they deny it.
rows.anchor: بالمصدر الجاري على الفعل إشارة إلى شدة العناية به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the previous sūra's account of revelation and its protection, this sūra prepares the Prophet for prophecy's burdens through intimate night communion, strengthening him for the work among the misguided.
rows.anchor: في آخر الجن من تعظيم الوحي وأن من تعظيمه حفظ المرسل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative form can address near or far and introduces only momentous matters; it signals the Prophet's intended nearness through extraordinary, superhuman tasks, while wrapping itself is ordinary preparation.
rows.anchor: بالأداة الصالحة للقرب والبعد المختصة بأنه لا يقال بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muzzammil evokes someone wrapped over the body, hidden and settled in one place; the source also links the root to carrying, bearing a burden, exertion, and strength.
rows.anchor: مدلوله التلفف في الثوب على جميع البدن والاختفاء ولزوم مكان واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assimilated tāʾ in al-muzzammil also gestures toward concealment, perhaps indicating that the garment did not cover the whole body, unlike the coming al-muddaththir address.
rows.anchor: ربما أشار الإدغام إلى أن الستر بالثوب لم يعم جميع البدن

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the address as one concealing the signs of spiritual distinction shown through him, whose time for disclosure has now come.
rows.anchor: يا أيها المخفي ما تظهره عليه من آثار الخصوصية

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the address as the one who has taken up this great matter.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذي حمل هذا الأمر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the address means O sleeper.
rows.anchor: السدي : أراد يا ألها النائم

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another view dates al-Muzzammil to the beginning of prophetic revelation and al-Muddaththir to the beginning of the messenger's public mission; later he was addressed as Prophet and Messenger.
rows.anchor: غيره : كان هذا في ابتداء الوحي بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qum calls the Prophet to serve God by bearing prophecy's burdens and exerting himself to carry them; rising requires leaving the wrapping behind.
rows.anchor: أي في خدمتنا بحمل أعباء نبوتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole night stands for a portion of every night; its privacy and concealment suit prayerful communion, and naming prayer signals the other outward and inward works it grounds.
rows.anchor: فأطلق اسم الكل وأراد البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night standing in Islamic law means prayer; Biqāʿī says it is unqualified here because prayer encompasses the other kinds of outward and inward worship and is their foundation.
rows.anchor: وقيام الليل في الشرع معناه الصلاة فلذا لم يقيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception allows the body some rest, while the command still concerns a portion of every night.
rows.anchor: ولما كان للبدن حظ في الراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, the frightened Prophet asked to be wrapped and feared for himself; Khadīja reassured him that God would not disgrace him, citing his care for kin and guests and aid to people in hardship.
rows.anchor: رجع إلى خديجة زوجته رضي الله تعالى عنها يرجف فؤاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrapping can gather a brave person's scattered faculties when a threat exceeds his strength, letting his sound nature overcome imagined disturbance and bodily distress.
rows.anchor: فائدة التزمل أن الشجاع الكامل إذا دهمه أمر هو فوق قواه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that after the jinn's acceptance and the failure of apparently more likely hearers to respond, the sūra turns to the Prophet's worship and night remembrances, opening with a gentle address that consoles him.
rows.anchor: مفتتحا ذلك بأجمل مكالمة وألطف مخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī continues Ibn al-Zubayr's coherence reading: Fāṭir 35:8, al-Maʿārij 70:5, al-Muzzammil 73:10–11, and Qāf 50:45 support patience amid opposition, followed by the warning of 73:12.
rows.anchor: وليحصل منه الاكتراث بعناد من قدم عناده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī sees a return to kindness toward the Prophet and companions, despite shortcomings in honoring God; 73:20 acknowledges that they cannot fully measure or fulfill the task and grants relief.
rows.anchor: ثم رجع الكلام إلى التلطف به عليه الصلاة والسلام وبأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra closes with seeking forgiveness for the disbelievers' earlier resistance and for what obedient believers fail to fulfill, as 73:20 indicates.
rows.anchor: ثم ختم السورة بالاستغفار من كل ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl means reciting calmly and articulating letters so the listener can count them; like well-spaced teeth, the measured recitation prompts reflection and discloses difficult meanings and hidden secrets.
rows.anchor: أي اقرأه على تؤدة وبين حروفه بحيث يتمكن السامع من عدها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd warns against scattering the Qurʾān like dates or rushing it like poetry; pause at its marvels, move hearts with it, and do not focus on reaching the sūra's end.
rows.anchor: ولا تنثروه نثر الدقل ولا تهذوه هذ الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating tartīl as a verbal noun emphasizes the honor and importance of measured Qurʾān recitation.
rows.anchor: أعلم بشرفه بالتأكيد بالمصدر

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet prayed through the night repeating one verse, which asks God to punish or forgive His servants and names Him Mighty and Wise.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام حتى أصبح بآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command sets a general manner of recitation beyond night prayer and shows that prayer's animating core is Qurʾān recitation.
rows.anchor: أمر بالقيام وقدر وقته وعينه , أمر بهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his community need steadfastness in prophethood's work and in following its commands and prohibitions; people cannot sustain this without divine aid and diligent service that purifies the soul.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد منه صلى الله عليه وسلم الثبات للنبوة ومن أمته الثبات في الاقتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic emphatic promise of soon casting a word upon the Prophet prepares him for a momentous burden; ʿalayka uses an elevated preposition to foreground its difficulty.
rows.anchor: أي بما لنا من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy word is the Qurʾān: its difficult obligations oppose human nature, its densely meaningful and majestic language requires deep thought, and opponents cannot refute or fault it; it is weighty in reception and in the scales.
rows.anchor: قولا } يعني القرآن { ثقيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although weighty, the Qurʾān is easy for the tongue, recitation, and memorization, as the promise that God made it easy for remembrance confirms.
rows.anchor: وهو مع ثقله على الأركان خفيف على اللسان سهل التلاوة والحفظ على الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ describes revelation making the Prophet sweat on a cold day; when it descended while he rode, his camel knelt and barely moved until revelation passed.
rows.anchor: وإن جبينه ليتفصد عرقا في اليوم الشاتي الشديد البرد

rows.speaker: القشيري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Sūrat al-Anʿām descended all at once while the Prophet rode, and his camel knelt under the Qurʾān's weight and awe.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
